cards.tp: The underlying pathophysiology in a patient that presents with poor vision for close-up objects (presbyopia) is decreased lens elasticity.

ww.Ciliary muscle paralysis: Ciliary muscle paralysis is not the usual cause; accommodation fails as the lens stiffens.
ww.Corneal flattening: Corneal flattening changes refractive power, not near focusing with age.

cards.evidence: The underlying pathophysiology in a patient that presents with poor vision for close-up objects (presbyopia) is decreased lens elasticity.

cards.tp: The recommended medication for treating Syphilis is Penicillin G, which is an antibiotic that is effective in treating all stages of the disease.

ww.Ciprofloxacin: Ciprofloxacin is not a treatment for syphilis; penicillin G is.
ww.Vancomycin: Vancomycin has no role in syphilis therapy.

cards.evidence: The recommended medication for treating Syphilis is Penicillin G, which is an antibiotic that is effective in treating all stages of the disease.

cards.tp: Ankylosing spondylitis is characterized by a "bamboo spine" appearance on X-ray.

ww.Rugger-jersey spine: Rugger-jersey spine is banded sclerosis of vertebral endplates seen in renal osteodystrophy.
ww.Codfish vertebrae: Codfish vertebrae are biconcave vertebrae of osteoporosis or sickle cell disease.

cards.evidence: Ankylosing spondylitis is characterized by a "bamboo spine" appearance on X-ray.

cards.tp: Multiple myeloma is associated with an elevated protein gap, with levels typically greater than 4 g/dL.

ww.Less than 1 g/dL: A gap under 1 g/dL is normal; myeloma produces excess globulin.
ww.About 2 g/dL: A modest gap of about 2 g/dL is normal, not a myeloma sign.

cards.evidence: Multiple myeloma is associated with an elevated protein gap, with levels typically greater than 4 g/dL.

cards.tp: NAPQI is the toxic intermediate that is formed in small amounts during the metabolism of acetaminophen.

ww.Acetaldehyde: Acetaldehyde is the toxic metabolite of ethanol.
ww.Formic acid: Formic acid is the toxic metabolite of methanol.

cards.evidence: NAPQI is the toxic intermediate that is formed in small amounts during the metabolism of acetaminophen.

cards.tp: The two most commonly associated gene mutations with hereditary breast cancer are BRCA1 and BRCA2.

ww.TP53 and PTEN: TP53 and PTEN are linked to Li-Fraumeni and Cowden syndromes, not typical hereditary breast cancer.
ww.APC and MLH1: APC causes familial polyposis and MLH1 causes Lynch syndrome.

cards.evidence: The two most commonly associated gene mutations with hereditary breast cancer are BRCA1 and BRCA2.

bw: Peripheral arterial disease stage III symptom
cards.tp: Stage III peripheral arterial disease (PAD) refers to a severe form of the condition, and the typical symptom associated with this stage is ischemic pain at rest.

ww.Intermittent claudication: Intermittent claudication is stage II; rest pain marks stage III.
ww.Asymptomatic: Stage III disease is symptomatic, not asymptomatic.

cards.evidence: Stage III peripheral arterial disease (PAD) refers to a severe form of the condition, and the typical symptom associated with this stage is ischemic pain at rest.

cards.tp: Epstein-Barr Virus is responsible for causing monospot positive infectious mononucleosis.

ww.Adenovirus: Adenovirus causes pharyngitis and conjunctivitis, not a positive monospot.

cards.evidence: Epstein-Barr Virus is responsible for causing monospot positive infectious mononucleosis.

bw: Temporal bone fracture that endangers the facial nerve
cards.tp: A transverse fracture of the temporal bone, which occurs along the short axis of the bone, is more likely to put the facial nerve at risk compared to a longitudinal fracture of the temporal bone.

ww.Longitudinal fracture: A longitudinal fracture is the more common type and less often injures the facial nerve.
ww.Comminuted fracture: A comminuted pattern describes fragments, not the facial-nerve-threatening orientation.

cards.evidence: A transverse fracture of the temporal bone, which occurs along the short axis of the bone, is more likely to put the facial nerve at risk compared to a longitudinal fracture of the temporal bone.

bw: Kidney cells that sense blood pressure
cards.tp: Juxtaglomerular cells are the type of cells in the kidney that detect changes in blood pressure.

ww.Macula densa cells: Macula densa cells sense distal sodium chloride, not pressure.

cards.evidence: Juxtaglomerular cells are the type of cells in the kidney that detect changes in blood pressure.

bw: Tumor evasion of CD8+ T cells
cards.tp: Tumor cells evade C 8+ T-cell immune surveillance by down-regulating MHC I expression.

ww.Downregulating PD-L1: Tumors do not benefit from losing PD-L1; they upregulate it to evade T cells.
ww.Secreting excess IL-2: Secreting excess IL-2 would enhance, not evade, T cell attack.

cards.evidence: Tumor cells evade C 8+ T-cell immune surveillance by down-regulating MHC I expression.

cards.tp: IgA protease cleaves IgA and allows for colonization of mucosal surfaces.

ww.Cleaves IgG: IgA protease does not cleave IgG.
ww.Degrades C3b: C3b degradation is not the function of IgA protease.

cards.evidence: IgA protease cleaves IgA and allows for colonization of mucosal surfaces.

cards.tp: Fragile X syndrome is the inherited disorder caused by the expansion of CGG trinucleotide repeats in the FMR1 gene.

ww.Friedreich ataxia: Friedreich ataxia is a GAA repeat disorder.
ww.Huntington disease: Huntington disease is a CAG repeat disorder.

cards.evidence: Fragile X syndrome is the inherited disorder caused by the expansion of CGG trinucleotide repeats in the FMR1 gene.

cards.tp: S. sanguinis belongs to the group of bacteria known as viridans streptococci.

ww.Group B streptococci: Group B streptococci are beta-hemolytic, not viridans.
ww.Enterococci: Enterococci are a separate genus from viridans streptococci.

cards.evidence: S. sanguinis belongs to the group of bacteria known as viridans streptococci.

cards.tp: The group of glomerular disorders characterized by proteinuria is called nephrotic syndrome, and the typical amount of protein excreted per day in this condition is greater than 3.5 g/day.
cards.evidence: The group of glomerular disorders characterized by proteinuria is called nephrotic syndrome, and the typical amount of protein excreted per day in this condition is greater than 3.5 g/day.

bw: Muscarinic receptor in SA and AV nodes
cards.tp: M2 muscarinic receptors are found in the atria, SA node, and AV node of the heart.

ww.M1: M1 receptors are mainly neuronal and gastric.
ww.M3: M3 receptors mediate smooth muscle contraction and glandular secretion.

cards.evidence: M2 muscarinic receptors are found in the atria, SA node, and AV node of the heart.

cards.tp: The upper one-third of the vaginal canal is derived from the Müllerian duct.

ww.Urogenital sinus: The urogenital sinus forms the lower vagina.
ww.Mesonephric duct: The mesonephric duct forms male internal genital structures.

cards.evidence: The upper one-third of the vaginal canal is derived from the Müllerian duct.

cards.tp: In the middle of the menstrual cycle, ovulation occurs, which happens 14 days prior to menses.

ww.7 days: Seven days is too short; the luteal phase lasts about 14 days.
ww.21 days: Twenty-one days is the midluteal timeframe, not ovulation timing.

cards.evidence: In the middle of the menstrual cycle, ovulation occurs, which happens 14 days prior to menses.

cards.tp: Ascending cholangitis is usually caused by ascending infection with enteric gram negative bacteria.

ww.Staphylococcus aureus: Staphylococcus aureus is not the usual cause of ascending cholangitis.

cards.evidence: Ascending cholangitis is usually caused by ascending infection with enteric gram negative bacteria.

cards.tp: Cystitis caused by Proteus mirabilis is characterized by alkaline urine (pH) with an ammonia scent.

ww.Acidic with fishy odor: Proteus urease makes urine alkaline, not acidic.
ww.Acidic with sweet maple-syrup odor: A maple-syrup odor suggests maple syrup urine disease.

cards.evidence: Cystitis caused by Proteus mirabilis is characterized by alkaline urine (pH) with an ammonia scent.

cards.tp: Trousseau Syndrome is a condition characterized by migratory thrombosis, specifically superficial thrombophlebitis.

ww.Hepatic vein thrombosis: Hepatic vein thrombosis is Budd-Chiari, not the classic Trousseau pattern.
ww.Cerebral sinus thrombosis: Cerebral sinus thrombosis is not the migratory Trousseau pattern.

cards.evidence: Trousseau Syndrome is a condition characterized by migratory thrombosis, specifically superficial thrombophlebitis.

cards.tp: Nystagmus is the ocular side effect associated with PCP intoxication.

ww.Ptosis: Ptosis is not a feature of PCP intoxication.

cards.evidence: Nystagmus is the ocular side effect associated with PCP intoxication.

cards.tp: Hemorrhagic cystitis is a genitourinary complication that can be caused by Adenovirus.

ww.Genital warts: Genital warts are HPV, not adenovirus.

cards.evidence: Hemorrhagic cystitis is a genitourinary complication that can be caused by Adenovirus.

cards.tp: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is an IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity reaction that is most often seen in individuals suffering from asthma or cystic fibrosis.

ww.Tuberculosis or sarcoidosis: ABPA is not tied to tuberculosis or sarcoidosis.
ww.Emphysema or lung cancer: ABPA is not tied to emphysema or lung cancer.

cards.evidence: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis is an IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity reaction that is most often seen in individuals suffering from asthma or cystic fibrosis.

cards.tp: Echinococcus granulosis (hydatid cysts) can be treated with albendazole.

ww.Ivermectin: Ivermectin is for strongyloidiasis and onchocerciasis.
ww.Metronidazole: Metronidazole treats anaerobes and protozoa, not hydatid cysts.

cards.evidence: Echinococcus granulosis (hydatid cysts) can be treated with albendazole.

cards.tp: The treatment for primary dysmenorrhea is NSAIDs, while the treatment for PMS is SSRI.

ww.Benzodiazepines: Benzodiazepines are not first-line for PMS.

cards.evidence: The treatment for primary dysmenorrhea is NSAIDs, while the treatment for PMS is SSRI.

cards.tp: The polyomavirus that can cause nephropathy is called the BK virus.

ww.JC virus: JC virus causes progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.
ww.Merkel cell polyomavirus: Merkel cell polyomavirus causes Merkel cell carcinoma.

cards.evidence: The polyomavirus that can cause nephropathy is called the BK virus.

cards.tp: In Riedel's thyroiditis, release of cytokines (e.g. TGF-β, IL-13) leads to fibroblast activation and fibrosis.

ww.IFN-γ and IL-12: IFN-γ and IL-12 drive Th1 responses.
ww.TNF-α and IL-2: TNF-α and IL-2 are not the fibrosis cytokines named here.

cards.evidence: TGF-β, IL-13) leads to fibroblast activation and fibrosis.

cards.tp: Preeclampsia with severe features is defined by a blood pressure reading of greater than 160/110 mm Hg.

ww.At least 140/90 mm Hg: At least 140/90 mm Hg defines hypertension in preeclampsia, not severe features.
ww.At least 180/120 mm Hg: At least 180/120 mm Hg is a hypertensive emergency threshold.

cards.evidence: Preeclampsia with severe features is defined by a blood pressure reading of greater than 160/110 mm Hg.

cards.tp: Activation of the inflammasome leads to increased production of IL-1B and IL-18.

ww.IL-6 and TNF-α: IL-6 and TNF-α are not the inflammasome products.
ww.IFN-γ and IL-12: IFN-γ and IL-12 are Th1 cytokines.

cards.evidence: Activation of the inflammasome leads to increased production of IL-1B and IL-18.

cards.tp: Fidaxomicin is an antimicrobial that inhibits the sigma subunit of RNA polymerase.

ww.DNA gyrase: DNA gyrase is the fluoroquinolone target.
ww.50S ribosomal subunit: The 50S subunit is hit by macrolides and linezolid.

cards.evidence: Fidaxomicin is an antimicrobial that inhibits the sigma subunit of RNA polymerase.

bw: Layer of skin where vitamin D3 forms
cards.tp: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is formed in the stratum basale layer of sun-exposed skin.

ww.Stratum corneum: The stratum corneum is dead keratinized cells.
ww.Stratum granulosum: The stratum granulosum is not the site of vitamin D3 synthesis.

cards.evidence: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) is formed in the stratum basale layer of sun-exposed skin.

cards.tp: The rapid diagnosis for a newborn with cataracts, failed hearing test, and continuous heart murmur is Congenital Rubella.

ww.Congenital toxoplasmosis: Congenital toxoplasmosis causes chorioretinitis and hydrocephalus.

cards.evidence: The rapid diagnosis for a newborn with cataracts, failed hearing test, and continuous heart murmur is Congenital Rubella.

cards.tp: Thiopental is a barbiturate with a rapid onset and duration of action due to high potency and high lipid solubility.

ww.Rapid renal excretion: Rapid renal excretion does not explain thiopental's short action.
ww.Rapid hepatic metabolism: Hepatic metabolism is slow; redistribution ends the effect.

cards.evidence: Thiopental is a barbiturate with a rapid onset and duration of action due to high potency and high lipid solubility.

bw: thin white fishy discharge, no inflammation
cards.tp: Bacterial vaginosis (Gardnerella vaginalis infection) is the cause of vaginitis that is characterized by a thin, white discharge with a fishy odor and no vaginal inflammation.

ww.Trichomoniasis: Trichomoniasis gives frothy yellow-green discharge with inflammation.

cards.evidence: Bacterial vaginosis (Gardnerella vaginalis infection) is the cause of vaginitis that is characterized by a thin, white discharge with a fishy odor and no vaginal inflammation.

bw: Spirochete in water contaminated by animal urine
cards.tp: The name of the spirochete found in water contaminated with animal urine is Leptospira interrogans.

ww.Borrelia burgdorferi: Borrelia causes Lyme disease via ticks.

cards.evidence: The name of the spirochete found in water contaminated with animal urine is Leptospira interrogans.

cards.tp: Orotic aciduria can be treated with UMP or uridine triacetate to bypass the mutated enzyme.

ww.Allopurinol: Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase, not pyrimidine synthesis.

cards.evidence: Orotic aciduria can be treated with UMP or uridine triacetate to bypass the mutated enzyme.

cards.tp: Midodrine may exacerbate supine hypertension.

ww.Torsades de pointes: Torsades is a QT-prolongation risk with other drugs.
ww.Hepatotoxicity: Hepatotoxicity is not the warning for midodrine.

cards.evidence: Midodrine may exacerbate supine hypertension.

cards.tp: If 2% of patients who receive a flu shot develop the flu, while 8% of unvaccinated patients develop the flu, the relative risk reduction is 0.75.

ww.25%: The relative risk reduction is the absolute difference divided by the control rate, not 25%.

cards.evidence: If 2% of patients who receive a flu shot develop the flu, while 8% of unvaccinated patients develop the flu, the relative risk reduction is 0.75.

bw: Renal enzyme releasing NH3 from glutamine
cards.tp: In the kidney, glutamine is broken down into NH3 and glutamate via the enzyme glutaminase.
cards.evidence: In the kidney, glutamine is broken down into NH3 and glutamate via the enzyme glutaminase.

bw: Glycolytic enzyme deficiency causing hemolytic anemia
cards.tp: Hemolytic anemia in newborns is commonly caused by a deficiency of the enzyme pyruvate kinase, which is involved in the process of glycolysis.

ww.Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase: G6PD is in the pentose phosphate pathway.
ww.Aldolase B: Aldolase B deficiency causes hereditary fructose intolerance.

cards.evidence: Hemolytic anemia in newborns is commonly caused by a deficiency of the enzyme pyruvate kinase, which is involved in the process of glycolysis.

cards.tp: The medical condition caused by the twisting of a portion of bowel around its mesentery is known as volvulus.
cards.evidence: The medical condition caused by the twisting of a portion of bowel around its mesentery is known as volvulus.

cards.tp: The immune overdrive seen in ARDS in patients with coronavirus may be related to cytokine storm.

ww.Complement deficiency: Complement deficiency does not cause immune overdrive.
ww.Selective IgA deficiency: IgA deficiency is an immune deficiency.

cards.evidence: The immune overdrive seen in ARDS in patients with coronavirus may be related to cytokine storm.

bw: RUQ pain after fatty meals, resolves within 6 hours
cards.tp: The likely diagnosis for the patient's condition is biliary colic.

ww.Acute cholecystitis: Cholecystitis pain lasts over 6 hours with fever.
ww.Acute pancreatitis: Pancreatitis causes epigastric pain radiating to the back.

cards.evidence: The likely diagnosis for the patient's condition is biliary colic.

bw: Pyrimidine base found only in DNA
cards.tp: The pyrimidine bases are cytosine, uracil, and thymine.
cards.evidence: The pyrimidine bases are cytosine, uracil, and thymine.

bw: Antibody screen in prenatal Rh testing
cards.tp: The test that is commonly used for Rh typing and antibody screening is the indirect Coombs test.

ww.Direct Coombs test: The direct Coombs test detects antibody on a patient's own RBCs.
ww.Kleihauer-Betke test: Kleihauer-Betke quantifies fetal cells in maternal blood.

cards.evidence: The test that is commonly used for Rh typing and antibody screening is the indirect Coombs test.

cards.tp: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase is regulated via negative feedback by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and AMP.

ww.Glucose-6-phosphate: Glucose-6-phosphate is a substrate or product, not the inhibitor.

cards.evidence: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase is regulated via negative feedback by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and AMP.

cards.tp: Pacinian corpuscles are the specific type of sensory receptors that sense both vibration and pressure.

ww.Merkel disc: Merkel discs detect sustained pressure and texture.

cards.evidence: Pacinian corpuscles are the specific type of sensory receptors that sense both vibration and pressure.

bw: Antibiotic class depositing in fetal teeth and bone
cards.tp: Tetracyclines are considered a teratogen and can deposit in fetal teeth and bone.

ww.Macrolides: Macrolides are not classically deposited in fetal teeth.
ww.Cephalosporins: Cephalosporins are generally safe in pregnancy.

cards.evidence: Tetracyclines are considered a teratogen and can deposit in fetal teeth and bone.

cards.tp: A condition that presents with segmental necrosis and breaks in glomerular basement membrane is likely to be Rapidly Progressive Glomerulonephritis (RPGN).

ww.Minimal change disease: Minimal change disease shows podocyte effacement without necrosis.

cards.evidence: A condition that presents with segmental necrosis and breaks in glomerular basement membrane is likely to be Rapidly Progressive Glomerulonephritis (RPGN).

cards.tp: Trichomonas vaginalis infection is associated with a yellow-green discharge.

ww.White and curdy: Yeast gives thick white curdy discharge.
ww.Thin gray-white: Thin gray-white discharge suggests bacterial vaginosis.

cards.evidence: Trichomonas vaginalis infection is associated with a yellow-green discharge.

cards.tp: Echocardiography is the imaging study that is used for the definitive diagnosis of cardiac tamponade.

ww.Chest X-ray: A chest X-ray may show a large heart but is not definitive.
ww.ECG: ECG may show electrical alternans but is not definitive.

cards.evidence: Echocardiography is the imaging study that is used for the definitive diagnosis of cardiac tamponade.

cards.tp: Bronchiectasis primarily affects the lower lobes of the lung.

ww.Upper lobes: Upper-lobe predominance fits cystic fibrosis and TB.
ww.Right middle lobe only: Right middle lobe alone is the Lady Windermere pattern.

cards.evidence: Bronchiectasis primarily affects the lower lobes of the lung.

bw: Hormone secreted by medullary thyroid carcinoma
cards.tp: Thyroid medullary carcinomas secrete calcitonin.

ww.Thyroglobulin: Thyroglobulin is made by follicular cells.

cards.evidence: Thyroid medullary carcinomas secrete calcitonin.

cards.tp: The autoimmune destruction of β islet cells, leading to hyperglycemia, is suggestive of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM).

ww.Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Type 2 diabetes involves insulin resistance, not autoimmune β-cell loss.
ww.Gestational diabetes: Gestational diabetes is pregnancy-related insulin resistance.

cards.evidence: As per the information provided, the autoimmune destruction of β islet cells, leading to hyperglycemia, is suggestive of Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM).

cards.tp: Mineralocorticoid excess (hyperaldosteronism) may cause metabolic alkalosis.

ww.Metabolic acidosis: Hyperaldosteronism causes metabolic alkalosis through H+ loss.
ww.Respiratory acidosis: Respiratory acidosis is a ventilation problem.

cards.evidence: Mineralocorticoid excess (hyperaldosteronism) may cause metabolic alkalosis.

bw: Smooth muscle band at arteriole-capillary junction
cards.tp: At the junction of the arterioles and capillaries is a smooth muscle band called the pre-capillary sphincter.

ww.Metarteriole: A metarteriole is the vessel that carries the sphincters, not the sphincter itself.
ww.Venous valve: A venous valve prevents backflow in veins.

cards.evidence: At the junction of the arterioles and capillaries is a smooth muscle band called the pre-capillary sphincter.

bw: Disease for which smoking is protective
cards.tp: Smoking is protective against ulcerative colitis.

ww.Celiac disease: Celiac disease is not improved by smoking.

cards.evidence: Smoking is protective against ulcerative colitis.

cards.tp: Trastuzumab is an IgG monoclonal antibody against the Her2/Neu receptor.

ww.EGFR: EGFR is the target of cetuximab.
ww.VEGF: VEGF is the target of bevacizumab.

cards.evidence: Trastuzumab is an IgG monoclonal antibody against the Her2/Neu receptor.

cards.tp: Theca-lutein cysts arise due to ovarian hyperstimulation secondary to markedly elevated β-hCG levels.

ww.Elevated prolactin: Prolactin does not drive theca-lutein cyst formation.
ww.Excess androgens: Excess androgens are linked to PCOS, not theca-lutein cysts.

cards.evidence: Theca-lutein cysts arise due to ovarian hyperstimulation secondary to markedly elevated β-hCG levels.

cards.tp: The conducting zone of the lung is responsible for warming, humidifying, and filtering the air.

ww.Gas exchange with blood: Gas exchange occurs in the respiratory zone.
ww.Surfactant production: Surfactant is made by type II pneumocytes in the respiratory zone.

cards.evidence: The conducting zone of the lung is responsible for warming, humidifying, and filtering the air.

bw: Nerve giving the palmar cutaneous branch
cards.tp: The palmar cutaneous branch arises from the median nerve, branches prior to the carpal tunnel, and travels above the transverse carpal ligament.

ww.Ulnar nerve: The ulnar nerve has its own palmar cutaneous branch but the named one arises from the median.
ww.Radial nerve: The radial nerve gives the superficial radial branch to the dorsal hand.

cards.evidence: The palmar cutaneous branch arises from the median nerve, branches prior to the carpal tunnel, and travels above the transverse carpal ligament.

cards.tp: Graves' disease is associated with Type II hypersensitivity reaction, which is antibody-mediated.

ww.Type IV: Type IV is T cell mediated delayed hypersensitivity.

cards.evidence: Graves' disease is associated with Type II hypersensitivity reaction, which is antibody-mediated.

cards.tp: The neurotransmitter acetylcholine is commonly decreased in individuals with Alzheimer's disease.

ww.Dopamine: Dopamine is reduced in Parkinson disease.
ww.Norepinephrine: Norepinephrine loss is not the key Alzheimer finding.

cards.evidence: The neurotransmitter acetylcholine is commonly decreased in individuals with Alzheimer's disease.

bw: Commonest cause of hypothyroidism where iodine is sufficient
cards.tp: The most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine replete countries is autoimmune or Hashimoto thyroiditis.

ww.Iodine deficiency: Iodine deficiency is the leading cause worldwide, not where iodine is sufficient.

cards.evidence: The most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine replete countries is autoimmune or Hashimoto thyroiditis.

bw: matched controls from the same cohort
cards.tp: The study design that starts with cohort studies and then followed by a case-control study where participants who develop an outcome of interest are selected as cases is called a nested case-control design.

ww.Retrospective cohort study: A retrospective cohort uses existing records of exposure and outcome.
ww.Cross-sectional study: A cross-sectional study measures exposure and outcome at one time.

cards.evidence: The study design that starts with cohort studies and then followed by a case-control study where participants who develop an outcome of interest are selected as cases is called a nested case-control design.

bw: Next acceptor of electrons from coenzyme Q
cards.tp: Electrons from coenzyme Q (ubiquinone) in the electron transport chain are transferred to complex III (Cyto b/c1).

ww.Complex IV: Complex IV receives electrons from cytochrome c, not directly from CoQ.
ww.Complex I: Complex I donates electrons to CoQ.

cards.evidence: Electrons from coenzyme Q (ubiquinone) in the electron transport chain are transferred to complex III (Cyto b/c1).

bw: Resistance to both cidofovir and foscarnet
cards.tp: Resistance to Cidofovir and Foscarnet occurs with mutations to viral DNA polymerase.

ww.Viral thymidine kinase mutation: Cidofovir does not need thymidine kinase, so TK mutations do not explain resistance.
ww.UL97 kinase mutation: UL97 kinase mutations cause ganciclovir resistance.

cards.evidence: Resistance to Cidofovir and Foscarnet occurs with mutations to viral DNA polymerase.

cards.tp: Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) is treated with albendazole.
cards.evidence: Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) is treated with albendazole.

cards.tp: Asbestos bodies contain iron, and they may be visualized using a Prussian blue stain.

ww.Periodic acid-Schiff: Periodic acid-Schiff stains glycogen and fungi.

cards.evidence: Asbestos bodies contain iron, and they may be visualized using a Prussian blue stain.

bw: Main local metabolic regulator of cerebral blood flow
cards.tp: The most important local metabolic factors for cerebral circulation are CO2 and H+ (pH).

ww.Sodium: Sodium does not regulate cerebral flow.
ww.Glucose: Glucose does not regulate cerebral flow acutely.

cards.evidence: The most important local metabolic factors for cerebral circulation are CO2 and H+ (pH).

bw: Leading cause of chronic pancreatitis in adults
cards.tp: Alcohol is the major cause of chronic pancreatitis in adults.

ww.Gallstones: Gallstones are the leading cause of acute pancreatitis, not chronic.
ww.Hypertriglyceridemia: Hypertriglyceridemia is a less common cause.

cards.evidence: Alcohol is the major cause of chronic pancreatitis in adults.

bw: bile duct, hepatic artery and which vessel
cards.tp: The portal triad consists of the bile duct, hepatic artery proper, and portal vein.

ww.Hepatic vein: The hepatic vein drains the liver, outside the triad.
ww.Central vein: The central vein sits in the middle of the lobule, not in the triad.

cards.evidence: The portal triad consists of the bile duct, hepatic artery proper, and portal vein.

cards.tp: Congenital risk factors for cataracts include disorders of galactose metabolism.

ww.Phenylketonuria: Phenylketonuria does not cause congenital cataracts.
ww.Maple syrup urine disease: Maple syrup urine disease does not cause cataracts.

cards.evidence: Congenital risk factors for cataracts include disorders of galactose metabolism.

cards.tp: On biopsy of a heart with myocarditis, a lymphocytic infiltrate with focal necrosis is highly indicative of viral myocarditis.
cards.evidence: On biopsy of a heart with myocarditis, a lymphocytic infiltrate with focal necrosis is highly indicative of viral myocarditis.

bw: Transfusion reaction with noncardiogenic pulmonary edema
cards.tp: Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI) is the type of blood transfusion reaction that presents with symptoms such as respiratory distress and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema.

ww.TACO: TACO is circulatory overload with cardiogenic edema.
ww.Anaphylaxis: Anaphylaxis presents with urticaria and bronchospasm.

cards.evidence: Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI) is the type of blood transfusion reaction that presents with symptoms such as respiratory distress and noncardiogenic pulmonary edema.

cards.tp: Glucose-insulinotropic peptide (GIP) is secreted from K cells located in the duodenum and jejunum.
cards.evidence: Glucose-insulinotropic peptide (GIP) is secreted from K cells located in the duodenum and jejunum.

ww.CT scan of the chest: A CT scan delays life-saving decompression.

cards.evidence: The recommended treatment for tension pneumothorax is needle decompression, which leads to thoracostomy (chest tube).

bw: Parasite in campers drinking untreated water
cards.tp: Giardia is the parasite commonly associated with individuals who go camping and do not purify their water before consumption.

ww.Cryptosporidium: Cryptosporidium needs acid-fast staining and affects immunocompromised patients.

cards.evidence: Giardia is the parasite commonly associated with individuals who go camping and do not purify their water before consumption.

bw: First synapse of cochlear nerve axons
cards.tp: All the axons in the cochlear part of CN VIII enter the pontomedullary junction and synapse in the ventral and dorsal cochlear nuclei.

ww.Superior olivary nucleus: The superior olivary nucleus is a later relay.
ww.Inferior colliculus: The inferior colliculus is a higher relay.

cards.evidence: All the axons in the cochlear part of CN VIII enter the pontomedullary junction and synapse in the ventral and dorsal cochlear nuclei.

cards.tp: A sprain of the Anterior Talofibular Ligament is classified as a low ankle sprain.

ww.High (syndesmotic) ankle sprain: A high ankle sprain involves the syndesmosis.
ww.Medial (deltoid) ankle sprain: A medial sprain involves the deltoid ligament.

cards.evidence: A sprain of the Anterior Talofibular Ligament is classified as a low ankle sprain.

cards.tp: Brief psychotic disorder is symptoms of schizophrenia lasting less than a month with more than one positive symptom.

ww.Schizoaffective disorder: Schizoaffective disorder has a mood episode component.

cards.evidence: Brief psychotic disorder is symptoms of schizophrenia lasting less than a month with more than one positive symptom.

ww.Membrane (M) protein: The membrane protein is the most abundant viral envelope protein.

cards.evidence: The helical nucleocapsid of coronavirus is a protein called N protein, which is bound to the RNA genome.

cards.tp: Somatostatinoma may present with diabetes due to inhibition of insulin.
